# Tomaz Fernandes

> Technical blog by Tomaz Fernandes, software engineer based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Lead maintainer for SQS in Spring Cloud AWS and AWS Community Builder. Writes about distributed systems: reliability, observability, messaging, and shipping small, reversible, production-safe changes.

## About the author

- **Name:** Tomaz Fernandes
- **Role:** Software Engineer (10+ years)
- **Location:** Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
- **OSS:** Lead maintainer for SQS in [Spring Cloud AWS](https://github.com/awspring/spring-cloud-aws). Rewrote the SQS integration in Spring Cloud AWS 3.0.
- **Spring contributions:** Contributed the [non-blocking delayed retries](https://docs.spring.io/spring-kafka/reference/retrytopic.html) feature in Spring for Apache Kafka.
- **Community:** [AWS Community Builder](https://builder.aws.com/community/@tomazfernandes).
- **Writing elsewhere:** Author of Spring Cloud AWS SQS articles on [Baeldung](https://www.baeldung.com/author/tomazfernandes).

## Canonical identities

- Website: https://tomazfernandes.dev/
- GitHub: https://github.com/tomazfernandes

- Baeldung author page: https://www.baeldung.com/author/tomazfernandes
- AWS Community Builder profile: https://builder.aws.com/community/@tomazfernandes

## What this site covers

- Distributed systems: reliability, observability, messaging, scalability
- Java and Spring-based backends
- AWS messaging (SQS, SNS) and Spring Cloud AWS internals
- Production-safe engineering practices

## Key pages

- [Home](https://tomazfernandes.dev/): landing page and recent posts
- [About](https://tomazfernandes.dev/about/): biographical details and links
- [All posts](https://tomazfernandes.dev/posts/): full archive
- [Examples](https://tomazfernandes.dev/examples/): runnable example projects for selected posts
- [RSS feed](https://tomazfernandes.dev/rss.xml)

## Posts

- [What Happens Between @SqsListener and Your Method](https://tomazfernandes.dev/posts/from-sqslistener-to-your-method/): walkthrough of the Spring Cloud AWS SQS message pipeline, from listener annotation through polling, conversion, invocation, acknowledgement, and error handling.

## Source repository

The site, posts, and example projects are open source at https://github.com/tomazfernandes/tomazfernandes-dev. Posts live in `/posts`, runnable examples in `/examples`, site source in `/site`.
